info.title: BigChalkBox Partner API
info.description: External server-to-server API: assignments, submissions, grading, metering.

get.description:
Auth smoke-check for integrators: proves the key works and shows
which client it resolves to.

Client identity plus the service account it acts as. v1 keys are
unscoped (every key can do everything), so `capabilities` documents
the surface rather than gating it.

Metering snapshot for this client's service account (plan + free-tier
usage counters). Read-only: enforcement of these limits on partner
routes arrives with Phase 1 — this endpoint lets platforms meter what
they resell before that. Usage counters live in the CORE database, so
this reads the core bridge, not the partner-local mirror.

schema.title: Response List Assignments Partner V1 Assignments Get

get.description:
Assignment detail — the bulk-generate poll endpoint: while
bulk_gen_status is RUNNING, bulk_gen_progress carries
{current, total, label} (checked on every read, and a job whose last
checkpoint is >3 min old is reconciled to FAILED here).

patch.description:
Partial update of a test's content fields and lifecycle status.
Status transitions DRAFT->ACTIVE and CLOSED->ACTIVE are NOT quota-gated
here (the UI's free-credit gate is a consumer-tier mechanism — partner
accounts meter via GET /usage; enforcement lands in Phase 1).

delete.description:
Delete a test and its stored answer sheets (DRAFT or CLOSED only —
an ACTIVE test must be closed first, so a stray call can't destroy a
live collection target).

put.description:
Full replace of the question set — same validation and canonical
materialization as create, so the grader's invariants (rubric per
subjective question, answers per MCQ) hold after any edit. Rubrics are
re-materialized together with questions because question-level rubrics
move with their questions.

Full replace of the rubric set. Stored as given; whether every
subjective question ends up covered is checked at grading time
(_grading_ready) so a partial rubric set can be staged across calls.

post.description:
Question-paper PDF -> structured questions. The paper is sent to
builder-ai's extraction pipeline over the internal network and the
result is passed through unchanged (questions, total_marks,
extraction_confidence, sections_meta).

The parse engine is resolved server-side from THIS client's
api_clients.parse_engine (Admin -> API Clients): an explicit "glm_ocr"
uses the self-hosted GLM-OCR hybrid read, anything else (null/
"default") the default vision path. The caller has no engine or
provider parameter (S2: AI control stays with us); flipping the admin
toggle takes effect on the client's next extract call.

Long by nature — a large paper can take tens of minutes (builder-ai's
worst case ~2800s; nginx's partner timeout covers it). Use a read
timeout of at least 30 minutes for this call.

Create a test from a Markdown paper template — deterministic,
zero-LLM, LINE-NUMBERED errors (FORMAT SPEC v1 lives in
paper_parser.py). The template carries the paper itself (question
text, marks, MCQ options) and, optionally, the answer key
(#### MODEL ANSWER / #### RUBRIC / #### MCQ ANSWERS sections).

A template without a key still creates the test — it just isn't
gradeable yet: complete it with POST /assignments/{id}/bulk-generate
(AI fills model answers, rubrics, MCQ correct answers) or add the key
sections and resend. Grading an uncovered question is refused with a
422 naming it, so nothing can grade silently.

Send either a .md/.markdown FILE or the md_text FORM field (not both).
Form title/subject/instructions override the file's '# <title>' /
'Subject: …' / 'Instructions: …' lines. Parse warnings (marks
mismatch, MCQs still missing answers) come back in the 201 body.

Fill in what the test is missing — SUBJECTIVE model answers +
rubrics, MCQ correct answers (flat or per sub-question) — with
builder-ai, one question at a time, in the background.

Answers 202 immediately; poll GET /assignments/{id} —
bulk_gen_status runs RUNNING → DONE | FAILED and bulk_gen_progress
carries {current, total, label} while running. Questions that are
already complete are skipped; an AI call that fails for one unit
skips that unit (the run still ends DONE — check what's missing
before grading). A second start while RUNNING is 409; a run whose
worker died is reconciled to FAILED after 3 quiet minutes.

get.description:
Gradebook for one test: every student's submission status and score,
newest-first by upload time (keyset-paginated on (submitted_at, id) DESC —
every partner-uploaded submission has submitted_at, unlike box-link rows
which are a Phase 1 feature). Per-question detail is not included; fetch
/submissions/{id}/results for that.

post.description:
Upload one student's answer sheet as a single PDF and (by default)
immediately queue it for AI grading. Mirrors the box upload flow
(dases_box.py) for storage keys, student upsert, and duplicate
handling — minus the hardcoded .edu email fallback: partners must
send an explicit email address.

get.description:
Score bands, problem areas and dashboard counts for one test.
Problem areas are the questions in the 3 worst DISTINCT average-score
tiers (DENSE_RANK, not a flat LIMIT — a tie at the cutoff keeps every
tied question). OR-group alternatives the student did not attempt
(skipped_or_alternative) are excluded so they cannot masquerade as
problem areas.

Server-built export (S1=B — we make the file):
format=xlsx — the results roster: every non-NOT_SUBMITTED student ×
  the paper's questions (marks obtained per question, Total Score),
  same columns and row order as teacher-web's Excel export (see
  exports.py for the parity contract).
format=zip  — one marked PDF per EVALUATED submission (OSM tests
  only), members named report_<Student_Name>_<id-prefix>.pdf.

post.description:
Upload a whole batch of answer sheets in one request. Per-file
identity, two ways (the explicit map wins):
  students — JSON object mapping EACH uploaded filename to
             {"email": ..., "name": ..., "enrollment_number": ...};
  email_domain — fall back to [ID]_[First]_[Last]_[extra].pdf parsing:
             email = <ID>@<domain>.
HTTP 200 with a per-file report even when some files fail (core
parity). Per-file outcomes:
  success — stored; queued (submitted_status QUEUED) when auto_grade
    and the answer key is grade-ready, otherwise SUBMITTED;
  error   — not a PDF, over 25MB, duplicate filename in the batch, an
    unresolvable identity, or an existing submission that is
    EVALUATED/PROCESSING/QUEUED (never replaced in flight or after
    grading — re-grade via POST /submissions/{id}/grade).
A SUBMITTED-but-ungraded existing submission IS replaced: the new
upload wins (same as core's teacher flow, same submission id + S3 key
so the old object is overwritten in place). Webhook:
submission.received per success, same transaction as the upload.

Queue (or re-queue) a submission for grading.
  mode=full (default) — re-run the whole pipeline (PDF -> pages ->
    classify -> grade); resets the current report. Use after uploading
    with auto_grade=false, or to re-grade after the assignment's rubrics
    were updated.
  mode=existing-pages — re-grade every question from the pages the last
    run already produced; skips render/classify/segmentation (the fast
    option, e.g. after a rubric or provider change). Requires EVALUATED;
    the report is preserved until the new run replaces it.
  mode=overrides — re-grade only the questions whose pages were
    rearranged via PUT /submissions/{id}/page-overrides, then the
    arrangement is baked into storage. Requires EVALUATED + a stored
    arrangement.
The fast modes are idempotent while a run is in flight (202), like
core's /reevaluate variants — `full` keeps 409 for a double-queue.

get.description:
Poll this until status is EVALUATED or ERROR — grading is
asynchronous. Webhook subscribers get grading.completed /
grading.failed pushed instead (POST /webhooks).
302 to a 1-hour presigned URL for the student's submitted PDF.

The graded page images grouped by question directory (q1, q2, …,
qMCQs), each with a 1-hour presigned URL. Reflects the post-grading
grouping — for OSM tests the annotated variants are what the
marked-PDF endpoint packs; the originals are listed here.

The page-rearrangement payload: the original full pages (no
sub-directory), the per-question page crops grouped by directory
(q1, q2a, qMCQs, …), and the stored override when one is active.
Every path also carries a 1-hour presigned URL — unlike core's
UI-relative media links, a partner can fetch pages directly.

put.description:
Store (or reset with enabled=false) a manual page arrangement.
`questions` maps a question number to the ORDERED list of page paths
it should grade from (an empty list = the question reads as not
attempted). Only changed questions need be sent. Re-grade with
POST /submissions/{id}/grade?mode=overrides.

get.description:
Streams a PDF of the OSM-annotated answer sheets (badge on page 1)
for tests created with osm_enabled=true — the visual 'returned sheet'.
Current subscription. Never returns the secret.

post.description:
Register (or fully replace) this client's webhook subscription.
The secret is shown exactly once, in this response.

patch.description: Partial update. The secret is returned only when it changed.

get.description: Newest-first delivery log — the client's redrive/debug view.

schema.title: Response List Webhook Deliveries Partner V1 Webhook Deliveries Get

post.description:
Re-queue a dead (or pending) delivery immediately. Delivered rows are
immutable history — 409.

get.description:
Unauthenticated probe for load balancers / uptime monitors. The
authenticated smoke-check for integrators is GET /partner/v1/health.

PartnerAssignmentAnalytics.title: PartnerAssignmentAnalytics
PartnerAssignmentAnalytics.description:
Port of core-api's per-assignment analytics (the headline numbers of
the teacher results page). Status counts cover the whole cohort; bands,
average and problem areas cover EVALUATED rows only. `pending` is the
residual (NOT_SUBMITTED + QUEUED), matching core.

PartnerAssignmentUpdate.title: PartnerAssignmentUpdate
PartnerAssignmentUpdate.description:
Partial update. Only the fields a partner owns — require_secure_login
and submission_mode are UI-only and not part of the external contract.
Toggling osm_enabled only affects FUTURE grading runs (re-queue a
submission to re-grade it with the new setting).

PartnerRosterItem.title: PartnerRosterItem
PartnerRosterItem.description:
One row of a test's gradebook. Deliberately excludes report_json —
per-student detail lives behind /submissions/{id}/results; pulling the
full report into a roster listing would make the page payload enormous.

QuestionIn.title: QuestionIn
QuestionIn.description:
One question of a partner-created assignment. The stored shape
mirrors the canonical questions_json the teacher UI produces (see
assignment_questions.json) so the grader reads it unchanged. Field
names model_answer/model_answers are the canonical storage names the
grader reads — hence the disabled pydantic model_ namespace.
